event.name: 2013 Sea of Okhotsk earthquake
event.summary: A deep earthquake beneath the Sea of Okhotsk, with paths beginning inside the mantle rather than near the surface.

stations.name: Matsushiro, Japan
stations.selection_reason: Japanese receiver selected for the nearest northern Pacific path.

observed_pick.recording_match: Station code matched. Upstream pick reports network IR and omits channel and location; it does not identify this particular BHZ trace. IU.00.BHZ is an independent open recording at the station and event-time epoch.

processing: Ignore zero-sample MiniSEED records and join exactly contiguous positive-sample records. No gaps are interpolated.
Convert raw integer instrumental counts to float64.
Remove the least-squares linear trend over the complete trace.
Apply a cosine taper to 2 percent at each end, limited to 30 seconds.
Apply a 4-corner, zero-phase Butterworth bandpass at 0.02 to 0.2 Hz.
Resample 20 Hz to 1 Hz with scipy.signal.resample_poly, up=1, down=20, window=('kaiser', 5.0), padtype='constant'. This includes an anti-alias FIR filter.
Round the displayed count samples to three decimal places. Preserve the raw MiniSEED separately.

provenance.credit: Albuquerque Seismological Laboratory/USGS (1988), Global Seismograph Network (GSN - IRIS/USGS), doi:10.7914/SN/IU. Recordings accessed through the EarthScope-operated data service. Manual P picks and event parameters from USGS ANSS phase data.

data_policy.basis: The IU DOI identifies Albuquerque Seismological Laboratory/USGS as creator. USGS-authored or produced data are in the U.S. public domain. Source attribution is retained.
data_policy.note: An empty DOI rights list is not a Creative Commons license declaration.

provenance.distance_convention: Spherical geographic great-circle distance without geocentric latitude correction.
limitations: Replay and path exploration only. No validated source-location exercise is provided for this event.
Catalog source depth and location are fixed historical references. IASP91 is a spherical one-dimensional model with surface receivers.
Only modeled P, S and PKIKP are supported. A missing modeled arrival is not proof that the real station recorded no seismic energy.
Manual P picks come from the archived USGS phase file. Stations without a unique manual P pick retain no observed pick.
An upstream pick reporting network IR without channel and location is matched by station code and event-time metadata. It does not identify this particular BHZ sensor.
Reported pick uncertainty is retained, including null values. A null uncertainty is not a claim of exact timing.
Filtered instrumental counts have no response removal. They are not calibrated displacement, velocity or acceleration, and amplitudes are not comparable between stations.
Zero-phase filtering can spread energy before an onset. The display filter and modeled times do not generate observed picks.
Model mismatch, finite source duration, Earth structure and phase-label differences can separate picks, visible signal and one-dimensional predictions.
